title: Semistability and geometric stability are invariant under field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension], and let $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ be a compatible pair of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] between multipointed $k$-curves [def-trf-multipointed-curve]. Compatibility means that the two maps commute with the closed marking immersions. A geometric fibre means base change [def-pc-fibre-product] to an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of the ground field [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Say $(Y,E)$ is geometrically semistable if each singular point of $Y_\Omega$ has completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $E$ is etale over $k$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $E$ lies in the smooth locus of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Say $f$ is geometrically stable if its source is geometrically semistable and no irreducible component of $Y_\Omega$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$, contracted by $f_X$, and meets the union of $E_\Omega$ and the singular points of $Y_\Omega$ in at most two points. Then $(Y,E)$ is geometrically semistable over $k$ if and only if its base change to $k'$ is geometrically semistable; and $f$ is geometrically stable over $k$ if and only if its base change to $k'$ is geometrically stable. The conditions are independent of the chosen algebraic closure; no generic-isomorphism or density assumption is needed.

source.place: §1.2, printed p. 2, geometric definition of semistability and exceptional components; Remark 3.1.1(i)(a),(ii), printed pp. 14--15, field-extension invariance required for approximation of diagrams.
